summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Zenith IO through the Redwood Console analytics and per-route cost breakdown. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated with interest in predictable cost and VPC options. Agreed next steps to run a short POC and exchange security docs.
transcript:
Header: 2025-10-22 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~42m | Attendees: Samantha (Redwood AE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Raj (Zenith Head of ML), Ava (Platform), Derek (CTO)

Summary: Quick console walkthrough focusing on usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and cost breakdown. Customer questions on batching, KV cache, and VPC private deployment.

[00:00] Samantha: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we got about 40 minutes on the calendar, should be enough to show the Console usage analytics and the per-route cost breakdown that you asked about.
[00:10] Raj: Yep thanks, we wanted to see the per-route detail, um, especially how you attribute cost to different product endpoints. We're looking to decide between hosted and dedicated.
[00:16] Carlos: Cool, I'll share my screen in a sec, quick intro on my side — I'm Carlos, I'm the solutions engineer, I work on the runtime and the batching side so I can answer deep infra questions.
[00:23] Ava: Great. we mostly care about tail latency under 200ms for our chat endpoints and cost per 1k tokens for embeddings workloads.
[00:30] Derek: Also want to confirm compliance posture, SOC two, KMS integration, and whether logs can be stored in our S3.
[00:36] Samantha: Noted. I'll flag those as we go; Carlos will show the dashboards and I'll jump in with pricing and contract options.

[02:01] Carlos: Alright screen's up. Starting on the Console home, top-level usage trends, you can see token volume by day, requests, avg latency. We'll jump to the per-route view — here we have routes instrumented, so you can see //chat.open and //embed.search — we tag by route, model, and client id.
[02:24] Raj: That tagging is good. Are those tags automatic or do we need to add headers in requests?
[02:30] Carlos: We support automatic route naming via the SDK and you can override with a route header, so it maps cleanly to product routes.

[03:15] Carlos: Now per-route dashboard: on the left is throughput and p95/p99 latency, center is token breakdown, right is cost. The cost column is calculated from per-token unit costs times actual token consumption, with adjustments for batching and caching heuristics.
[03:37] Ava: Wait, how do you handle KV cache or prefix cache? Does that reduce billable tokens?
[03:42] Carlos: Good question. We don't bill for tokens served from the KV cache in the same way; you get effective token savings because the runtime serves fewer compute tokens. In the console cost model we show both gross tokens and billed tokens, so you can see the delta.
[04:05] Raj: Any typical delta numbers? Like what reductions should we expect for conversational history caching?
[04:10] Carlos: It depends, for our bench we've seen 20% to 60% reduction depending on prompt reuse patterns. For high-reuse chat it's usually 40% on average.

[05:00] Samantha: On pricing, for hosted it's per-token with tiered discounts as volume increases; for Dedicated you have reserved GPU pools and a commit for predictable throughput. We'll send the exact tiers after the call.
[05:25] Derek: For dedicated, what's the scaling model? Does it auto-scale if we spike?
[05:30] Carlos: We support burst capacity and configurable autoscale policies. Reserved capacity gives you baseline throughput and you can opt into burst credits for short spikes.

[06:30] Raj: How is multi-model routing handled? If a request exceeds latency SLO we want fallback to a cheaper smaller model.
[06:40] Carlos: We have smart routing rules — you can route by latency or cost policy. Console shows route-level policies and historical fallbacks. If you set fallback to a quantized variant, it swaps automatically.

[08:05] Carlos: Back to analytics, you can split by model family or hardware region. This is helpful to see if a specific route is more expensive because it's using a larger model or because of long sequences.

[09:15] Ava: Can we export the raw per-request events to our data lake?
[09:20] Samantha: Yes, audit logs and request traces can be exported. We also have a raw events dump for usage analytics that can be S3-delivered or streamed to your warehouse.

[10:00] Raj: About encryption — does Redwood support customer-managed keys?
[10:05] Carlos: Yep KMS/HSM integration is supported for Private deployments and Dedicated we can integrate with your KMS via key wrapping. For hosted we have managed keys but can discuss bring-your-own-key for enterprise.

[11:10] Derek: For SOC 2, can you share where the logs are retained and whether we can get separate retention settings per route? We have some PII concerns.
[11:20] Samantha: We will share SOC 2 docs and the retention options; you can also configure redaction rules per route — we can redact payloads before they land in logs. We'll attach the security pack after this call.

[12:30] Carlos: Jumping to the cost breakdown view: here's a sample month for one route — total tokens, billed tokens, cost per token, and the cumulative cost. The Console lets you attribute cost to teams by setting a 'client id' dimension.
[12:55] Raj: Can we also see cost by feature? e.g., billing chat feature A separately from chat feature B?
[13:00] Carlos: Yes if you instrument routes per feature or set metadata keys, you can slice that in the console. The analytics is flexible.

[14:30] Ava: Curious about the latency distribution. The p95 looks fine, but p99 spikes are concerning. Is that typically queuing or long seq lengths?
[14:40] Carlos: Often it's long sequences or cold KV cache misses. The console has a trace link — you can click into the p99 spike and see sequence length distribution and whether it was served from cold cache or required compilation.

[16:00] Samantha: I wanted to show the cost simulation tool — you can model different batching and quantization profiles and see projected cost changes. So if you move a route to a quantized 4-bit variant you can project ~30-40% cost savings depending on workload.
[16:20] Raj: How accurate are those projections? We need them to be realistic for finance planning.
[16:26] Carlos: They're based on historical runtime metrics and kernel throughput profiles. For steady-state patterns the projections are within 10-15% typically. We always recommend running a short POC to validate.

[18:00] Derek: For POC, what's needed from our side? Data, traffic replay?
[18:05] Carlos: Ideally a representative traffic sample and a small dataset. We can run replayed requests in a sandbox dedicated pool; we'll run both latency and cost profiling.

[19:15] Raj: We have a lot of internal regulation — if we go dedicated or private, can we get audit logs pushed to our SIEM?
[19:23] Samantha: Yes SIEM integration via push or S3 is supported for Dedicated and Private. Hosted can deliver logs but for strict regulatory needs Private is recommended.

[20:40] Ava: About integration: our infra uses k8s with VPC peering; does Redwood support peering and private endpoints?
[20:48] Carlos: Yes we do VPC peering and private endpoints in Private and Dedicated configurations. For Hosted we provide regional endpoints; Private gives you customer-managed networking.

[22:00] Carlos: Quick note on model catalog: Console shows verified performance profiles per model — latency, tokens/sec, best hardware. That makes picking the right variant easier.

[23:30] Raj: Any mention of competitors — are you seeing customers move off from OpenAI to Redwood for cost reasons?
[23:38] Samantha: Some customers choose Redwood for predictability and on-prem options. Others still use a mix; we integrate with multiple model backends where needed.

[25:00] Carlos: Walkthrough of an example: route /chat/assist had 3.2M tokens, billed 2.1M after caching, cost $1,800 for the month. The console showed which user segments drove most cost.
[25:20] Ava: Nice, that level of granularity will help our product managers.

[27:10] Derek: About SLA — what uptime & latency SLOs are offered for Dedicated?
[27:18] Samantha: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; specific numbers depend on contract tier, we'll include details in the pricing PDF.

[29:00] Carlos: One more advanced piece: automatic fallback policies — you can set rules to fall back to a cheaper quantized model on high load, and the Console shows historical fallback rates and cost savings.

[30:20] Raj: For the POC window, can we try both hosted and dedicated comparatives? We want apples-to-apples.

[30:30] Carlos: Yes we can run both side-by-side — hosted sandbox vs dedicated reserved pool — same traffic replay and measure cost and latency.

[32:10] Ava: Will the POC require a contractual commit for dedicated? We want trial capacity without long-term lock-in.
[32:18] Samantha: We have short-term reserved trials and flexible pilot options. We'll outline those in the follow-up.

[34:00] Raj: Any gotchas with token counting? We've seen differences between providers.
[34:06] Carlos: We use a consistent tokenizer; the console reports gross vs billed tokens and shows the tokenizer used. Differences usually come from whitespace or different tokenizers; we can match your tokenizer if needed for fair comparison.

[35:30] Derek: About data residency — can we restrict region for logs and model inference?
[35:36] Samantha: Yes region pinning is supported for Private and Dedicated. Hosted can be pinned to specific cloud regions as well. We'll include region options in the security doc.

[37:00] Raj: Great. I'd like to recap next steps.
[37:04] Samantha: Sure, recap: we'll send pricing and committed/dedicated options; Carlos will send the benchmark checklist and sample workload script; we'll attach SOC2 and architecture diagram; Raj will confirm POC dataset and SLOs and we'll schedule the POC for early November.
[37:20] Raj: Perfect. Who will be our main contact on Redwood?
[37:24] Samantha: I'll be your AE, Carlos is the SE. You'll get intros to infra SE for peering.

[38:10] Ava: Couple quick questions — about per-route retention, can we set different retention at route level?
[38:15] Carlos: Yes you can configure retention/redaction per route in Private and Dedicated; for hosted there are defaults but enterprise can get per-route controls.

[39:00] Derek: Okay if you send the docs we'll review and propose a POC timeline.
[39:05] Samantha: Sounds good. We'll follow up by Friday with the materials.

[40:00] Raj: Thanks all, that was helpful.
[40:05] Carlos: Thanks everyone.
[40:06] Samantha: Thanks, bye.

Action items in transcript: Samantha to send pricing and security pack by 2025-10-24; Carlos to share benchmark script; Raj to confirm dataset and SLOs.

Notes: transcription contains small mis-hears (e.g., SOC two sometimes transcribed as S-O-C two), occasional speaker label glitches typical of Fireflies exports. Links referenced: Pricing deck (link: /redwood/pkgs/pricing-zenith-io.pdf), Security pack (link: /redwood/security/soc2-2025.pdf), Benchmark checklist (link: /redwood/benchmarks/zenith-checklist.xlsx).
